correctness.rationale: Checked RESULT.md lines 4–33. At n=3 there are no forbidden triples, even with h. At n=4,5 the deletion is a simplex and the link is the cycle. For n≥6 each selected proper cycle subset induces a union of paths; five vertices force an independent triple and four avoid one exactly when matched by two disjoint cycle edges. All smaller admissible faces extend to those facets. Gale evenness gives exactly those facets of the cyclic 4-polytope, including wraparound. The simplicial pushout along the actual link is the mapping cone of a null map S¹→S³. The natural exact sequence identifies H₂ with the link's orientation line and H₃ with the deletion's. For the asserted integral top cycle, a ridge consisting of an edge and an isolated vertex has the two completions at the predecessor/successor of the isolated vertex, which delete opposite positions of the oriented second edge. A ridge consisting of three consecutive vertices has the predecessor/successor completions deleting the first/last position of the oriented four-vertex string. In both cases the coefficients cancel. Each facet occurs once with unit coefficient; reflection reverses both edge blocks, so fixes the generator, whereas it reverses the link. This proves the actual signs without any claim about equivariant wedge equivalence. The recorded finite checker was inspected, not executed; its dimension/rank checks do not certify the all-n proof or the H₂ action.
residual_risks: No equivariant homotopy assertion or formal proof assessment.
